verdicts.title: On the automorphism group of a distance-regular graph
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: The motion of a graph is the minimal degree of its full automorphism group. Babai conjectured that the motion of a primitive distance-regular graph on $n$ vertices of diameter greater than two is at least $n/C$ for some universal constant $C > 0$, unless the graph is a Johnson or Hamming graph. verdicts.title: Automorphism and outer automorphism groups of Right-angled Artin groups are not relatively hyperbolic
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We show that the automorphism groups of right-angled Artin groups whose defining graphs have at least 3 vertices are not relatively hyperbolic. We then show that the outer automorphism groups are not relatively hyperbolic, if they are not virtually isomorphic to a right-angled Artin group whose defining graph is either a single vertex or disconnected.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns relative hyperbolicity of automorphism groups of right-angled Artin groups, which shares only the vocabulary 'automorphism group' with the conjecture but says nothing about |Aut(G)| order or communication complexity rank variance for d-regular graphs.
